entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Martin I of Sicily, called the Younger, was King of Sicily from his marriage to Queen Maria in 1390 until his death in 1409. A member of the House of Antioch, Martin I played a crucial role in Sicily's complex web of alliances and rivalries during the late Middle Ages. His reign was marked by tensions with neighboring kingdoms, including the Kingdom of Naples and the Republic of Venice. Martin I's policies aimed to strengthen Sicily's economy and military, but ultimately, his kingdom succumbed to the growing power of the Kingdom of Aragon. Despite this, Martin I's legacy as a capable and ambitious ruler has endured in Sicilian history. His rule was also marked by the devastating effects of the Black Death, which ravaged Sicily in the early 14th century. Martin I's response to the pandemic included measures to improve public health and support those affected. The King's efforts to mitigate the disaster were seen as a testament to his compassion and leadership. Through his policies and actions, Martin I of Sicily left a lasting impact on the island of Sicily and the surrounding regions. His reign serves as a reminder of the complexities and challenges faced by medieval kingdoms in the face of war, disease, and economic uncertainty.
